advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _windows_pid_alive answer alive without a call for any pid below 4 (not only pid <= 0), and add 1-3 to the non-positive-pid test's parameters
evidence: src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py:288: "or below answers alive without a call: ``OpenProcess`` also fails with 87 for pid 0 (the"
src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py:289: "System Idle Process), and a corrupt stamp must never earn a liveness-based reclaim."
src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py:413: "if not _pid_alive(pid):" followed by "return True" (stale -> reclaim)
Real Windows pids are multiples of 4, so os.getpid() never stamps 1-3. Those values can only come from a corrupt or hand-made stamp, which is exactly the case the guard is meant to cover.
advisory.finding: The `pid <= 0` guard in _windows_pid_alive covers pid 0 but not pids 1-3. Windows ignores the low two bits of a pid when it looks up a process id. If that holds, OpenProcess(1..3) resolves to the same slot as pid 0 and fails with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87). A corrupt stamp with pid=1, 2 or 3 would then read 'not-running' and earn the liveness-based reclaim the docstring says must never happen.
scenarios: A torn or corrupt same-host v2 stamp, or a legacy `host:1` stamp, on Windows reads not-running, and the mkdir lock or staging dir is reclaimed without proof.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the guard to `if pid < 4: return True` (or `pid <= 0 or pid & 3`, since no real Windows pid has its low bits set). Update the docstring and test_a_non_positive_pid_is_alive_without_a_call to match.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In spawn_python, open a SYNCHRONIZE handle to the interpreter pid on Windows and keep it alive until after the test's dead-pid assertions, so the pid cannot be recycled
evidence: tests/_python_child.py:10: "* Windows reuses a freed pid quickly. A \"dead\" pid stays reserved only while some handle to"
tests/_python_child.py:29: "_REAPED: list[subprocess.Popen] = []" is filled only by dead_pid(); spawn_python/stop never pin the interpreter pid
advisory.finding: spawn_python hands back the venv interpreter's pid (the launcher's child), but nothing holds a handle to that process. On Windows its pid can be recycled as soon as the interpreter exits. The helper's own docstring says Windows reuses a freed pid quickly. stop() then polls `_pid_alive(pid)` and can hit a recycled pid and spin to the 30s AssertionError. test_probe_answers_a_lock_held_by_another_process asserts `pid_state=not-running` after stop() and can read a recycled live pid. Only dead_pid() pins its pid, and in that case the pinned pid is the launcher's.
scenarios: On a busy Windows CI worker, another process takes the freed interpreter pid between its exit and the poll or assertion, so the test fails or times out intermittently.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make spawn_python/stop keep the interpreter's pid reserved after it exits, e.g. by holding a SYNCHRONIZE handle to it on Windows, just as dead_pid() keeps its Popen in _REAPED.
evidence: tests/_python_child.py docstring: "Windows reuses a freed pid quickly. A \"dead\" pid stays reserved only while some handle to the exited process is open."
dead_pid() keeps the handle open: "_REAPED.append(proc)". spawn_python/stop never append to _REAPED, and behind a venv launcher `proc` is the launcher, not the interpreter whose pid is returned.
stop() returns as soon as `lock_owner._pid_alive(pid)` reads False. At that point nothing in the test holds a handle to the interpreter, so its pid is free to be reused.
tests/unit/test_write_lock_busy_probe_7084.py:130: "stop(proc, pid)" is followed at line 135 by: assert "pid_state=not-running" in _lock.describe_lock_holder(str(tmp_path))
The diff deletes .github/windows-sweep-deselect/pid-liveness.args, which deselected test_probe_answers_a_lock_held_by_another_process, so the test now gates on Windows.
advisory.finding: spawn_python()/stop() do not keep a handle to the interpreter process, so after stop() Windows can reuse the stopped holder's pid. test_probe_answers_a_lock_held_by_another_process asserts `pid_state=not-running` for that pid after stop(), which can flake on the Windows sweep this diff re-enables.
scenarios: Windows CI: the holder interpreter is terminated, stop() sees it dead, another process on the runner gets the same pid, and describe_lock_holder reports it live or unverified-live, failing the not-running assertion.
advisory.suggested_fix: On Windows, have spawn_python open a SYNCHRONIZE | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION handle to the reported interpreter pid (via lock_owner._load_kernel32) and keep it in a module-level list for the rest of the session, as _REAPED does for dead_pid. stop() still waits for the pid to read dead (WAIT_OBJECT_0), and the open handle stops Windows reusing the pid before the later not-running assertion.
